name: Report
description: A Report object refers to a particular Microsoft Access report.
remarks: A Report object is a member of the Reports collection, which is a collection of all currently open reports. Within the Reports collection, individual reports are indexed beginning with zero. Refer to an individual Report object in the Reports collection either by referring to the report by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. If the report name includes a space, the name must be surrounded by brackets ([ ]).
example:
Private Sub Report_NoData(Cancel As Integer)

    'Add code here that will be executed if no data
    'was returned by the Report's RecordSource
    MsgBox "No customers ordered this product this month. " & _
        "The report will now close."
    Cancel = True

End Sub

methods.name: Circle
methods.signature: Circle(flags As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single, radius As Single, color As Long, start As Single, end As Single, aspect As Single)
methods.description: The Circle method draws a circle, an ellipse, or an arc on a Report object when the Print event occurs.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Indicates the radius of the circle, ellipse, or arc. The Scale properties (ScaleMode, ScaleLeft, ScaleTop, ScaleHeight, and ScaleWidth) of the Report object specified by the Object argument determine the unit of measure used. By default, distances are measured in twips.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Indicates the RGB (red-green-blue) color of the circle outline. If this argument is omitted, the value of the ForeColor property is used. You can also use the RGB function or QBColor function to specify the color.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: When a partial circle or ellipse is drawn, the Start argument specifies (in radians) the beginning position of the arc. The default value for the Start argument is 0 radians. The range is -2 pi radians to 2 pi radians.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: When a partial circle or ellipse is drawn, the End argument specifies (in radians) the end position of the arc. The default value for the End argument is 2 pi radians. The range is -2 pi radians to 2 pi radians.

parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: Indicates the aspect ratio of the circle. The default value is 1.0, which yields a perfect (nonelliptical) circle on any screen.

methods.name: Line
methods.signature: Line(flags As Integer, x1 As Single, y1 As Single, x2 As Single, y2 As Single, color As Long)
methods.description: The Line method draws lines and rectangles on a Report object when the Print event occurs.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Indicates the RGB (red-green-blue) color used to draw the line. If this argument is omitted, the value of the ForeColor property is used. You can also use the RGB function or QBColor function to specify the color.

methods.name: PSet
methods.signature: PSet(flags As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single, color As Long)
methods.description: The PSet method sets a point on a Report object to a specified color when the Print event occurs.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: A keyword that indicates that the coordinates are relative to the current graphics position given by the settings for the CurrentX and CurrentY properties of the Object argument.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The horizontal coordinate of the point to set.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The vertical coordinate of the point to set.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The RGB (red-green-blue) color to set the point to. If this argument is omitted, the value of the ForeColor property is used. You can also use the RGB function or QBColor function to specify the color.

methods.name: Scale
methods.signature: Scale(flags As Integer, x1 As Single, y1 As Single, x2 As Single, y2 As Single)
methods.description: The Scale method defines the coordinate system for a Report object.

parameters.name: x1

parameters.name: y1
parameters.description: A value for the vertical coordinate that defines the position of the upper-left corner of the object.

parameters.name: x2
parameters.description: A value for the horizontal coordinate that defines the position of the lower-right corner of the object.

parameters.name: y2
parameters.description: A value for the vertical coordinate that defines the position of the lower-right corner of the object.

events.name: Error
events.signature: Error(DataErr As Integer, Response As Integer)
events.description: The Error event occurs when a run-time error is produced in Microsoft Access when a report has the focus.

parameters.name: DataErr
parameters.description: The error code returned by the Err object when an error occurs. Use the DataErr argument with the Error function to map the number to the corresponding error message.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description:
The setting determines whether or not an error message is displayed. The Response argument can be one of the following intrinsic constants:
  • acDataErrContinue Ignore the error and continue without displaying the default Microsoft Access error message. You can supply a custom error message in place of the default error message.
  • acDataErrDisplay (Default) Display the default Access error message.

events.description: The NoData event occurs after Microsoft Access formats a report for printing that has no data (the report is bound to an empty recordset), but before the report is printed. Use this event to cancel printing of a blank report.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines whether to print the report. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) prevents the report from printing. You can also use the CancelEvent method of the DoCmd object to cancel printing the report.

events.name: Page
events.description: The Page event occurs after Microsoft Access formats a page of a report for printing, but before the page is printed. Use this event to draw a border around the page, or add other graphic elements to the page.

events.description: The LostFocus event occurs when the specified report loses the focus.

events.name: Click
events.description: The Click event occurs when the user presses and then releases a mouse button over a report.

events.name: DblClick
events.description: The DblClick event occurs when the user presses and releases the left mouse button twice over a report within the double-click time limit of the system.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the DblClick event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) cancels the DblClick event.

events.name: MouseDown
events.signature: MouseDown(Button As Integer, Shift As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single)
events.description: The MouseDown event occurs when the user presses a mouse button.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
The button that was pressed to trigger the event. If you need to test for the Button argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acLeftButton The bit mask for the left mouse button.

  • acRightButton The bit mask for the right mouse button.

  • acMiddleButton The bit mask for the middle mouse button.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the Button argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The x coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The y coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

events.name: KeyDown
events.signature: KeyDown(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyDown event occurs when the user presses a key while a report has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a report by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting KeyCode to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: KeyPress
events.description: The KeyPress event occurs when the user presses and releases a key or key combination that corresponds to an ANSI code while a report has the focus. This event also occurs if you send an ANSI keystroke to a report by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyAscii
parameters.description: Returns a numeric ANSI key code. The KeyAscii argument is passed by reference; changing it sends a different character to the object. Setting the KeyAscii argument to 0 cancels the keystroke so that the object doesn't recognize that a key was pressed.

events.name: KeyUp
events.signature: KeyUp(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyUp event occurs when the user releases a key while a report has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a report by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting KeyCode to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the Shift argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: Timer
events.description: The Timer event occurs for a report at regular intervals as specified by the report's TimerInterval property.

events.name: Filter
events.signature: Filter(Cancel As Integer, FilterType As Integer)
events.description: Occurs when the user opens a filter window by choosing Advanced Filter/Sort.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines whether to open the filter window. Setting the Cancel argument to True (1) prevents the filter window from opening. You can also use the CancelEvent method of the DoCmd object to cancel opening the filter window.

parameters.name: FilterType
parameters.description: The filter window the user is trying to open. The FilterType argument can be acFilterAdvanced.

events.name: ApplyFilter
events.signature: ApplyFilter(Cancel As Integer, ApplyType As Integer)
events.description: Occurs when a filter is applied to a report.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the ApplyFilter event occurs. Setting the Cancel argument to True cancels the ApplyFilter event and the filter is not applied to the report.

parameters.name: ApplyType
parameters.description: Returns the type of filter that was applied.

events.name: MouseWheel
events.signature: MouseWheel(Page As Boolean, Count As Long)
events.description: Occurs when the user rolls the mouse wheel in Report view or Layout view.

parameters.name: Page
parameters.description: True if the page was changed.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: The number of lines by which the view was scrolled with the mouse wheel.
